correctness.rationale: Generalized Hall gives exact optimal kappa approvals to each agent; rank-two count gives kappa>=floor(d/2); n>=3 permits distributing every remaining good to a nonapprover; the total outside approvals of any agent bound cross-bundle envy by one, hence complete EQ+EF1 (and EQ+EF for even degree). In exact-two multigraphs m=nd/2 fixes kappa, exact welfare gap and parity; Euler orientations prove the full efficiency alternatives. Includes d=0, loops forbidden, parallel goods permitted, odd n-degree parity, and n=2 counterexample. The standalone 362-instance-type and 18 small exhaustive-allocation checks passed; they are finite corroboration, not an infinite proof.

value.rationale: Nonlaminar sparse binary approval markets form an important family beyond the laminar condition in the motivating 2026 paper. The theorem guarantees an optimal exactly equitable and EF1 allocation for unbounded populations, and measures the full sharp utilitarian price of demanding exact equity when all goods have two approving agents. A Pareto-optimal approximate-equity alternative restores all lost welfare, explaining a structural parity-driven efficiency/fairness tradeoff.
